title: firefox web performance and WebGL2RenderingContext.getParameter
body: ### Tested versions reproduced in 4.6.2, don't have earlier versions available to me right now ### System information linux mint 22.3, firefox 150 ### Issue description Had really weird performance problems with a game, spent a long time debugging it, eventually realized it was nothing to do with the game. I can reproduce this with a node2d containing a label, with a _process() that sets label.text to the current FPS. using Firefox, with integrated graphics, I get about 45-50 FPS if my window is full-screen, and 60 if it's half-screen, on a 4k monitor. This might be a performance issue with the video card, but I note that it works fine in Chrome on the same exact setup, and the profile looks WEIRD. I've attached a screenshot of the profile. I thought "maybe it's pixel fill rate" and expected the time to be going into blitting. It's not. It's going into WebGL2RenderingContext.getParameter(), which is getting 58-60% of all CPU time in my profiles. ### Steps to reproduce export HTML5, upload to itch.io, view in Firefox. I've done all the usual things to ensure that firefox is using hardware acceleration, and it seems like it is? Nothing else I've tried is slow like this. It is possibly relevant that the display I'm on is 3840x2160 and firefox is only a few pixels short of full screen. If I make the firefox window half this size, it's fine. Chrome works fine at any size, and nothing else I've done in Firefox has had any problems. I'm unclear on why getParameter is getting called that much at all -- don't most of the things it would return rarely change? Or is it being used to extract the texture or something? Anyway it seems weird to me. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) Here's a minimal project. It really is just one line of writing text into a label. [performance_2026-04-21_17-58-33.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26949276/performance_2026-04-21_17-58-33.zip)
